messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D pixel-art roguelike platformer for phones and tablets about animal travelers managing homesickness while exploring biomes and towns.

## Requirements
- Homesickness rises from revisiting areas and hardships, falls from visiting sights, and resets in each new town.
- Towns offer purchasable wandering equipment; animals have distinct advantages and disadvantages.
- Support mobile/tablet touch controls and 16-bit-era graphics; build without clarification.

## Decisions
- Implemented a self-contained HTML Canvas game with hand-drawn pixel-style graphics and no external assets.
- Added three selectable travelers (fox, bear, rabbit), four biomes/towns, sights, puddles/thorns, shop equipment, and a final ending.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created a playable game in `index.html` with keyboard and touch controls, home/lost/ending states, town shop, and equipment effects.
- Checked JavaScript syntax with `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved screenshots; visual review was performed for title, mobile, and world views.

### Active
- None.

### Blocked
- Browser check command sequence for holding a movement key failed with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'new'`; a follow-up screenshot was taken, but this did not validate extended gameplay or town progression.

## Next Move
1. Optionally test gameplay progression, shop purchases, and mobile touch input in-browser.
2. Review `git status` and report final changed files; changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/title.jpg`: Title screen capture.
- `screenshots/mobile.jpg`: Mobile viewport capture.
- `screenshots/world.jpg`: Gameplay capture.

## Important Context
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` succeeded after installing Chromium; initial console error was only a missing favicon and a data-URI favicon was subsequently added.
- The intended game has keyboard controls (arrows/A-D, Space/Up, E) and touch controls drawn on the canvas.

## Little Elsewhere is ready to play

I built the game in `index.html` as a self-contained pixel-art Canvas game, with no external assets. It includes three animal travelers with different traits, four biomes, sights that ease homesickness, hardships and purchasable gear, new towns between levels, and an ending.

**Controls:** Arrow keys or A/D to move, Space or Up to jump, and E to explore. On touchscreens, use the on-screen controls; landscape orientation gives the game more room.

I checked the JavaScript syntax and opened the game in a browser to review its title, mobile, and gameplay views. I didn’t complete an automated end-to-end check of town progression or purchases. My assumption was that “rogue-like” meant a short replayable journey rather than procedurally generated runs.

metadata.displayText: I would like the game renamed to "Wanderlust." I want the graphics to be more 16-bit era rather than 8-bit (super Nintendo rather than NES). The movement and jumping should feel smoother and tighter. Make more vertical area as well, so players feel like they are climbing up to a spectacular view. The views should be goals, not collectables. Make "small wonders" along the way, a berry bush, a rare flower, etc. that restore wanderlust. Change the homesickness bar into the wanderlust bar that goes down as homesickness increases (homesickness is no longer visibly measured. Internally, treat wanderlust and homesickness as a percentage. Visiting sights and seeing "small wonders" increase wanderlust, whereas things that cause homesickness decrease Wanderlust
